div.ab: Of a prudent reeve [of a great estate].
div.note: Liebermann's text is from B (Cambridge, Corpus Christi College 383, p. 102, after Rect, same hand, c. 1125), the same manuscript as the modern edition; Liebermann treats Gerefa as the continuation of Rect (see Rect 1). There is no Quadripartitus version. The heading is in red. Perhaps the original read ‘Gescadwis’ (Zupitza); B often drops ‘ge-’ (compare 17b).; F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date in the running heads), October 2026 (was “960 (c.1025?) – 1060; ?Bath Abbey (Wormald)”, now “960 (c.1025)–1060 (Liebermann); ?Bath Abbey (Wormald)”); F: corrected against Liebermann, Gesetze I (date at the head of the text); Wormald, Making of English Law I; Whitelock, English Historical Documents I, October 2026 (was “960 (c.1025)–1060 (Liebermann); ?Bath Abbey (Wormald)”, now “960 (c.1025)–1060 (Liebermann, I p. 453); ?Bath Abbey (Wormald)”); BQ: page of each of Liebermann’s texts and of his German, checked against Liebermann, Gesetze I (our double-read transcription), October 2026 (e.g. was “(empty)”, now “B 453; German 453”; 31 rows of Ger)
